title: A Simple and Efficient Estimator for Hyperbolic Location
subtitle: Core Argument Plan: Two-Step Weighted LS for TDOA Localization

nodes.title: Problem Definition & Existing Limitations
nodes.purpose: Define the hyperbolic location problem using TDOA measurements and identify limitations of existing methods (iterative Taylor-series requiring initial guess, non-optimum closed-form SI/SX, DAC noise threshold issues).

nodes.title: Mathematical Formulation & Noise Model
nodes.purpose: Establish the nonlinear distance equations relating sensor positions, source coordinates, and TDOA. Define the statistical properties of TDOA estimation errors (Gaussian, covariance matrix Q).

nodes.title: Equation Transformation to Linear Form
nodes.purpose: Explain the core mechanism: transforming nonlinear hyperbolic equations into a set of linear equations in source coordinates (x, y) and an intermediate variable (range r1) by subtracting reference sensor equations.

nodes.title: First Step: Unconstrained Weighted LS
nodes.purpose: Derive the initial solution by treating x, y, and r1 as independent variables. Apply generalized Least Squares (LS) using the approximate covariance matrix to solve for these parameters.

nodes.title: Second Step: Constraint Enforcement
nodes.purpose: Incorporate the known geometric relationship between coordinates and the intermediate variable (r1^2 = x^2 + y^2) via a second weighted LS step to refine the estimate and achieve optimality.

nodes.title: Variance Analysis & CRLB Comparison
nodes.purpose: Derive the theoretical covariance matrix of the position estimate using perturbation analysis. Prove that the estimator attains the Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) in the small error region.

nodes.title: Special Case: Linear Array Geometry
nodes.purpose: Address the singularity issue in linear arrays. Show how the method reduces to a specific solvable form identical to prior optimum solutions (Abel & Smith) for this configuration.

nodes.title: Simulation Results: Near-Field Performance
nodes.purpose: Present empirical MSE comparisons against SI and Taylor-series methods for arbitrary and linear arrays with near sources, confirming theoretical accuracy and CRLB attainment.

nodes.title: Simulation Results: Far-Field & Thresholds
nodes.purpose: Demonstrate performance with distant sources. Highlight the higher noise threshold compared to the Divide and Conquer (DAC) method and robustness against divergence compared to Taylor-series.

nodes.title: Computational Complexity & Explicit Solution
nodes.purpose: Summarize the computational advantages: non-iterative nature, explicit closed-form solution, and avoidance of local minima problems inherent in iterative methods.

coverage_notes: The argument flows from problem definition (nonlinear equations) to the core innovation (two-step LS with intermediate variable), followed by theoretical proof (CRLB) and empirical validation (Simulations).
Pages 3-4 contain the critical derivation of the two-step estimator (Eq 14a, 22a).
Pages 8-10 provide the necessary evidence for performance claims (Tables I-IV, Fig 4).
The distinction between arbitrary and linear arrays is handled as a specific branch in the logic (Section II-B).
